faq: Do you test with real payments?
No. We use the payment provider's test mode and test cards, or a real order we refund at once if you ask. Your customers are never charged during testing, and we never use anyone else's card.
Do you need the old store as well?
For Standard and Premium, yes, view access to the old store lets us compare products and orders. For Basic we only check the new store, so the old store access is optional.
Will you tell me if the store is not ready?
Yes, plainly. The Premium report ends with a go or no-go view and the reasons. If something serious is wrong, we say so and show what must be fixed first.
Is this the same as a speed or SEO audit?
Only in part. We spot check speed and search titles so launch problems show up. Full audits are separate services and go into much more detail.

desc:
Pre-launch store testing and QA means checking your new store as a shopper would, before the domain is switched. Ecom Swift LLC walks through the purchase journey, compares data with the old store and gives you a ranked list of issues, with quick fixes made.

## What is pre-launch store testing?

Pre-launch testing is a structured pass through the new store to find faults while only your team can see them. It covers the shopping path, the data that was moved, emails, forms, menus and how pages look on different devices.

QA stands for quality assurance. The aim is a short, honest report of what works, what does not and what to fix first.

## Why testing before launch is worth the effort

A store that has never been used by a stranger hides mistakes. A discount code that stacks wrongly, a variant that cannot be selected on a phone, a contact form that sends nowhere: these do not show up in a settings screen. They show up when a real customer tries.

Finding them before launch is cheaper than finding them after. After launch you lose orders and trust and spend time apologizing. Before launch, a fault is just a task.

## How testing protects revenue and reputation

The purchase path is where money is made, so each step has to work. We check that products can be added to the cart, shipping options appear, discounts apply and payment completes. A fault in any of these quietly turns visitors away.

Quality also shapes first impressions. Broken images, missing descriptions and menus that lead nowhere make a store look unfinished. Comparing a sample of products with the old store catches moved data that is wrong, such as prices, variants or images that did not carry across.

## What a thorough test includes

- A checklist of key checks, from home page to order confirmation.
- Testing on desktop and mobile views, and across browsers in the deeper package.
- A sample comparison of products against the old store.
- Cart behavior with several items, quantities and variants.
- Discount codes and gift cards used at checkout.
- Test payments with test cards, never real ones.
- Order and customer emails received and read.
- Contact and newsletter forms submitted.
- Links, menus and footer pages clicked.
- Page speed and image checks.
- A spot check of search titles and redirects.
- A go or no-go summary at the end of the top package.

## What we do

We agree a test plan with you and ask for a preview link or staff access to the new store. We then go through the store as new shoppers, in the order they would. Every fault is logged with a screenshot and a note on how to reproduce it.

Issues are ranked: stop-ship problems first, then things that should be fixed soon, then small polish points. In Standard and Premium packages we fix the quick ones ourselves, such as a broken link or a wrong label. After you or your developer correct the larger items, the Premium package includes a retest.

You receive a clear verdict. If the store is not ready, we say so.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep the old store available for side-by-side checks.
- Test on your own phone as well as ours.
- Use realistic orders, including odd ones.
- Fix the issues in order of importance.
- Retest after every large change.

**Avoid:**
- Treating a quick look as a test.
- Testing only the best-selling product.
- Skipping emails because they seem minor.
- Launching with open stop-ship issues.
- Fixing symptoms in several places instead of the cause.

## Who this is for

An owner or agency who has just finished building a store and wants a second pair of eyes. A seller with a tight launch date who needs a clear go or no-go answer. A business moving a large catalog where small data errors are likely.

## What we need from you

A preview link or staff access to the new store, test payment details if your provider supplies them, and the old store address for comparison. Tell us which journeys matter most.

We never ask for passwords, and we do not use real payment cards. Access is limited to the roles needed to test, and you can remove it once we are done.
